title: Cost-Latency-Trust Triangle: Core Positioning Brief
summary: A concise internal brief that frames Redwood as the inference platform that helps engineering teams navigate tradeoffs across cost, latency, and trust. Introduces the 'Triangle' as a central narrative device for sales and content, and provides messaging hooks, proof points, and rebuttals for common buyer objections.
mission_statement: Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference a predictable engineering primitive — one that teams can buy, operate, and measure without rebuilding the infra economics or compromising trust.
thesis: Buyers don’t choose models; they choose predictable outcomes. Teams facing volatile token costs, inconsistent latency, and operational risk will prefer a vendor that treats inference as an engineering service with measurable SLAs, cost controls, and transparent failure modes. By owning the serving surface and developer experience, Redwood can turn inference from an experimental cost center into a predictable platform leverage point.
why_redwood: Redwood is uniquely positioned because we combine three concrete capabilities that buyers care about: 1) runtime optimizations that reduce per-token cost and tail latency, 2) deployment flexibility (hosted, dedicated, private) so customers balance isolation and economics, and 3) observability + policy controls that translate model behavior into ops-level SLOs. Together these form a practical guarantee: teams can deliver LLM features within cost, latency, and compliance constraints without hiring a separate inference org.
positioning_points:
1) The Triangle framing: every inference decision sits at the intersection of Cost, Latency, and Trust (security/consistency). Redwood is the platform that lets teams move the needle on all three — not by sacrificing one for another, but via knobs, fallbacks, and transparent tradeoffs.
2) Developer-first contracts: same API and rollout tools across hosted, reserved, and private deploys so product owners can ship without platform rewrites.
3) Measurable outcomes: token-level billing, per-route latency percentiles, regressions tied to eval prompts — metrics you can build SLAs around.
4) Practical fallbacks: model variants, region routing, and automatic quality-aware failover reduce blast radius during incidents.
customer_pain_points:
1) Unpredictable spend after ramp — spike in token usage that finance can’t forecast.
2) Latency spikes that break UX (search, chat, code completion).
3) Compliance and data residency needs that large cloud APIs can’t satisfy.
4) Ops overhead to tune batching, caching, and quantization — teams keep reimplementing the same patterns.
5) Fear of silent quality regressions after model/quantization changes.
differential_evidence:
1) Runtime wins: internal benchmarks showing 20–35% token-cost reduction on common seq-length distributions vs standard endpoints (workload-specific kernels and KV cache reuse).
2) Deployment parity: public case study where a customer moved from hosted to dedicated capacity with <24h config change and no customer-facing regressions.
3) Observability: example dashboard screenshots (latency by token, cache-hit rates) and an eval-alert demo that flagged a prompt regression during a model rollout.
4) Economics story: sample math for a mid-market customer showing 12-month TCO reduction when using reserved capacity + smart batching vs naive hosted consumption.
messaging_hooks_for_sales:
1) For platform/infra leads: 'Turn inference into a predictable SLA-backed primitive that your app teams can consume.'
2) For product leaders: 'Ship features that rely on low tail latency without hiring a full inference team.'
3) For finance/security: 'Get transparent token-level accounting and private deployments; no surprises and no data exfiltration.'
4) Rapid demo angle: show a live tail-latency improvement and a cost delta for a 1M-token workload.
objection_handling_snippets:
Objection: 'We can self-host and save money.'
Response: 'Self-hosting trades capital and ops risk for uncertain savings. Redwood gives you repeatable, workload-aware optimizations and an ops playbook we’ve validated across customers — plus options to transition between hosted and private so you can capture savings without long experiments.'
Objection: 'We need on-prem air-gapped deploys.'
Response: 'Redwood Private supports air-gapped workflows with a customer-controlled control plane and KMS/HSM integrations; we provide an on-prem package and rollout playbook used by regulated customers.'
suggested_marketing_lines:
1) 'Predictable inference: control cost, cut latency, keep trust.'
2) 'Turn LLMs into an SLA-backed engineering primitive.'
3) 'Same API. Same ops. All deployment choices.'
